div.head: IV Eg 6.1
div.ab: ⁊ heora ælc, þonne hine man ærest to witnysse gecysð, sylle þæne að, þæt he næfre, ne for feo ne for lufe ne for ege, ne ætsace nanes þara þinga, þe he to gewitnysse wæs, ⁊ nán oðer þingc on gewytnesse ne cyðe buton þæt án, þæt he geseah oððe gehyrde.

⁊ heora ælc, þonne hine man ærest to wytnesse gecysð, sylle þone að, þæt he næfre, ne for feo ne for lufe ne for ege, ne ætsace nanes þara þinga, þe he to gewytnesse wæs, ⁊ nan oðer þingc on gewytnesse ne cyðe butan þæt án, þæt he geseah oððe gehyrde.

Quique huic iustificationis operi fuerit electus et prepositus, iuret quod nullo modo, deprauatus pecunię muneribus nec alicuius amore uel timore seductus, quicquam aliud testificare uelit nisi quę auribus audierit aut oculis uiderit, uel negare presumat quod factum pro certo scierit.

⁊ heora ælc, þonne hine man ærest to wytnesse gecysð, sylle þone að, þæt he næfre, ne for feo ne for lufe ne for ege, ne ætsace nanes þara þinga þe he to gewytnesse wæs, ⁊ nan oðer þingc on gewytnesse ne cyðe butan þæt án þæt he geseah oððe gehyrde.

And each of them, when he is first chosen as a witness, shall swear an oath that he will never, for money, or favour or fear, deny any of the things of which he has been witness, or declare in his testimony anything except only what he has seen or heard.

And each of them, when he is first chosen as a witness, is to take an oath that never, for money or love or fear, will he deny any of the things for which he was a witness, and will never declare anything in his testimony but that alone which he saw and heard.

Und jeder von den [Geschäfts-Zeugen], wenn er zuerst zur Zeugenschaft erkoren wird, leiste folgenden Eid: ‘dass er nie, weder für Geld, noch aus Liebe, noch aus Furcht keines der Dinge, wo er als Zeuge [zugezogen] war, ableugnen werde, und nichts anderes im Zeugniss aussagen werde, als allein das, was er gesehen oder gehört hat’.

And let each of [these transaction-witnesses], when he is first chosen as a witness, swear the following oath: ‘that he will never, neither for money nor for love nor for fear, deny any of the things to which he was a witness, and will declare nothing else in his witness except only what he saw or heard’.
